scope: Review 25 semantic candidates and 20 active questions across Chapters 11–12. Preserve natural-experiment assumptions, numerical comparisons, attribution and source wording.

questions.reason: 把疑问当研究假说，不以儿童造成地震等荒谬选项凑数。

options: Whether prosocial children were less likely to experience an earthquake.
Whether the earthquake may have changed children’s perspectives and prosocial tendencies.
Whether a change in children’s values had already been established for every child.
Whether Fujimoto rather than the earthquake caused the children’s change in outlook.
optionsZh: 亲社会儿童是否更不容易经历地震。
地震是否可能改变儿童的人生视角和亲社会倾向。
是否已经确立每个儿童的价值观都发生改变。
是否是 Fujimoto 而非地震造成儿童视角变化。
analyses: A 原句询问经历地震后的可能变化，不是用亲社会程度预测谁会遭遇地震。
B is it possible...changed...and made... 明确提出视角与亲社会倾向可能改变的问题。
C is it possible 是疑问，没有宣布每位儿童都已改变的结论。
D As with... 是类比，不把 Fujimoto 说成这些儿童变化的直接原因。

questions.reason: 区分as if randomly、presumably和实际随机分派；同批纵向追踪并非当前句所给假设。

options: The researchers randomly allocated earthquake exposure to the two groups.
All background differences were measured and shown to be absent.
The same children provided the pre- and post-earthquake observations.
The groups were presumed comparable apart from experiencing the earthquake.
optionsZh: 研究者把地震暴露随机分派给两组。
所有背景差异都经过测量，并被证明不存在。
震前和震后的观察来自同一批儿童。
除经历地震外，推定两组在其他方面可比。
analyses: A as if randomly 是仿佛随机，不是研究者实际安排地震暴露。
B presumably 表示假定，不是把所有背景变量都测量并证实完全相等。
C 本句表达两条件间可比性的假定，没有说是同一批个体纵向追踪，不能把可比等同于个体相同。
D 括号说明 presume no other differences except earthquake experience；保留 sort of 和 as if 的设计限定。

evidence.quote: This created a sort of natural experiment where participants in the pre- and post-earthquake conditions were chosen as if randomly (meaning the children in the pre-earthquake study were presumably no different from the children in the post-earthquake study in any other ways except for having experienced the major earthquake).

questions.reason: 数字干扰围绕均值、分母与时间方向；证据补齐震前和震后一月时点。

options: From about four of ten before the earthquake to slightly over one afterward.
From slightly over one of one hundred to about four of one hundred.
From slightly over one of ten to about four of ten.
From slightly over one of ten to exactly two of ten for every child.
optionsZh: 从震前十张中约四张，变为震后略多于一张。
从一百张中略多于一张，变为约四张。
从十张中略多于一张，变为约四张。
从十张中略多于一张，变为每名儿童都恰好两张。
analyses: A 将震前和震后一月的两个均值颠倒。
B 两句都说 out of the ten stickers，不能把分母改为一百。
C before...slightly more than one 与 one month after...about four 保留均值、近似程度和方向。
D 震后平均约四张，不是两张；on average 也不能变成每个儿童同一精确数值。捐赠计数是行为测量，不是自陈利他。

evidence.quote: Before the earthquake, nine-year-olds gave, on average, slightly more than one out of the ten stickers.
One month after the earthquake, nine-year-olds gave, on average, about four out of the ten stickers.

questions.reason: 用作者解释限定made的因果措辞，不把感染观察改成随机感染或治疗建议。

options: The author interprets personal COVID-19 experience as shifting values prosocially.
Existing prosocial values are said to have caused the personal COVID-19 experience.
Only those without personal COVID-19 experience are said to have changed values.
The change described is in disease symptoms rather than in personal values.
optionsZh: 作者把 COVID-19 的个人经历解释为使价值观朝亲社会方向改变。
既有亲社会价值观被说成造成了 COVID-19 的个人经历。
被说成价值观改变的仅有无 COVID-19 个人经历者。
所述改变是疾病症状，而非个人价值观。
analyses: A 直接保留原句作者用 made 作出的解释；当前单句没有独立因果识别设计，不能自行升级为随机感染试验。
B 颠倒作者所述方向，本句不是用既有价值解释如何获得疾病经历。
C personal experience...made...victims... 与该项的人群方向不同。
D change their values 是明确对象，不是症状改善。此处讨论书中解释，不提出感染或医学治疗建议。

questions.reason: 去掉原选项中未明示的精确先后，把反向解释保留为外出、死亡焦虑、丰富性与感染风险的一种可能联系。

options: Infection may first reduce death anxiety and then lead to a more active life.
The paragraph rules out any link between activity and the chance of infection.
Getting out without death anxiety may explain both a richer life and greater infection risk.
Greater death anxiety may be what drove the most active people to go out more.
optionsZh: 感染可能先降低死亡焦虑，再带来更活跃的生活。
本段排除了活动与感染概率之间的任何联系。
不带死亡焦虑地外出，可能同时解释更丰富的生活与较高感染风险。
更强的死亡焦虑可能驱使最活跃的人更多外出。
analyses: A 这是感染在先、生活变化在后的方向，不是此处另提的反向可能。
B more likely to get COVID 明确保留外出与感染机会之间的联系。
C people who were getting out...without death anxiety 同时有更丰富生活、也更可能感染，为感染造成丰富性之外提供一种可能解释；不补造各变量的精确测量时序。
D without death anxiety 不是更强的死亡焦虑驱动外出。possible 也没有把另一解释证明为唯一原因。

questions.reason: 完整引文补齐角色视角与叙述层面，正确项保留sounds和most likely，不当客观人生事件或直接测量。

options: A change in perceived role alters what actually happened rather than merely the account.
The observer’s role is presented as the only route to a more meaningful story.
Perceived role affects how the story sounds; greater psychological richness is described as likely.
Psychological richness is treated as a measured fact identical to life satisfaction.
optionsZh: 所感知角色的改变会改动实际发生的事，而不只是叙述。
旁观者角色被说成让故事更有意义的唯一途径。
感知到的角色影响故事听起来怎样；更高心理丰富性被说成很可能出现。
心理丰富性被当作与生活满意度完全相同的已测事实。
analyses: A how the story is told 与 sounds 指叙述及其呈现，不是改变已发生的事实。
B hero or observer 是视角对照，没有 only route 的唯一途径判断。
C 保留 perceived role 对叙述的关系、sounds 的呈现层面及 most likely 的保留语气。
D 三个维度并列不等于相同，心理丰富部分还有 most likely，不能写成此处直接测量的确定事实。

evidence.quote: Ultimately, the way you view your role in your own life—whether you see yourself as a hero of the story or as an observer— does make a difference in terms of how the story is told and whether your life sounds more satisfying, more meaningful, and, most likely, psychologically richer.

questions.reason: elaborate是对发生事件详细加工，不暗示虚构细节；保留注意、反复思考与展开三个要素。

options: Notice the event, revisit it often, and consider it in detail.
Revisit others’ descriptions without attending to the event yourself.
Attend to the event once, then set it aside without further reflection.
Elaborate on an imagined event instead of attending to what happens.
optionsZh: 注意事件，经常回想，并仔细思考其细节。
反复看别人的描述，但自己不注意事件。
仅注意事件一次，然后搁置而不再反思。
详细展开想象事件，而不注意实际发生什么。
analyses: A pay attention、think...frequently 和 elaborate 分别对应注意、经常回想和详细加工。
B 原句要求 we pay attention，不能以反复听别人描述来排除自己的注意。
C think...frequently 不等于看过一次就不再思考。
D what is happening 与 an event 是加工对象，不要求把想象内容当成发生过的事实。in order to 表记忆目的，不保证永不遗忘。
